digest.headline: UK inflation rose to 3.5% as the pound climbed and the Reserve Bank of India rejected all bids at its Treasury bill auction.

lede.b: United Kingdom inflation reached 3.5% in September due to higher fuel costs. Inflation means that prices for everyday items go up over time. This higher price growth made the pound currency strengthen against the dollar and euro. Investors now think the Bank of England will raise its interest rate in November. Interest rates act like the cost of borrowing money across the economy.
lede.i: UK inflation accelerated to 3.5% in September driven by rising fuel prices. This hotter-than-expected reading immediately pushed sterling higher against the dollar and the euro as traders priced in a November rate hike by the Bank of England. The stronger currency and higher rate expectations weighed down the FTSE 100 equity index. Meanwhile, domestic data showed no immediate sign of broader second-round wage effects.
lede.a: UK headline inflation printed at 3.5% for September on surging fuel components, prompting an immediate repricing of Bank of England rate expectations. Sterling appreciated against both the dollar and the euro while the FTSE 100 compressed under the dual weight of currency appreciation and tighter rate paths. The absence of broader second-round wage feedback loops remains the core assumption for the current pricing structure.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: UK inflation rises to 3.5% as fuel costs climb

stories.t: UK Inflation Accelerates to 3.5% in September
stories.b: UK inflation measures how fast the prices of everyday goods and services go up over time. Government figures show that annual inflation accelerated to 3.5% in September. Surging fuel prices pushed the rate higher ahead of the upcoming national budget. Higher fuel costs drove the unexpected jump in consumer prices.
stories.i: UK inflation accelerated to an annual rate of 3.5% in September. Surging fuel prices drove the faster pace of price growth ahead of the Autumn Budget. Analysts had anticipated a lower reading before the official data release.
stories.a: UK headline inflation printed at 3.5% for September, overshooting consensus expectations. Surging fuel costs, exacerbated by the conflict involving Iran, served as the primary transmission vector for the upward surprise ahead of the Autumn Budget.

stories.t: Pound Strengthens and Stocks Slip Following Inflation Data
stories.src: Global Banking & Finance Review · Yahoo Finance UK
stories.b: The pound is the currency used in the United Kingdom. Sterling climbed against both the dollar and the euro after the inflation figures came out. Traders now expect interest rates to rise sooner. Meanwhile, the FTSE 100 stock index declined.
stories.i: Sterling climbed against the dollar and the euro as the hotter-than-expected price data fueled bets on a November rate hike by the Bank of England. The FTSE 100 equity index declined in response to the stronger currency and rate expectations. Markets saw no immediate sign of broader second-round wage effects in the economy.
stories.a: Sterling rallied against the dollar and the euro as the headline print catalyzed immediate repricing of Bank of England policy paths for November. The FTSE 100 drifted lower as the stronger currency weighed on constituent multinationals. Underlying price pressures showed no concrete evidence of second-round feedback loops.

politics.i: The Autumn Budget approaches while officials confront the fiscal implications of rising consumer prices.
politics.a: Policymakers navigate impending fiscal announcements in the Autumn Budget against a backdrop of accelerating consumer prices.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Tourism spending records and currency updates

stories.t: Foreign Visitor Spending Reaches Record High
stories.b: People who visit Japan from other countries spend money on hotels, food, and gifts. This spending helps local shops and businesses grow. Between January and September, this foreign spending hit a record 7 trillion yen. This means travelers spent more money in Japan during these months than ever before.
stories.i: Foreign visitor spending reached a record 7 trillion yen between January and September. International travelers contributed significantly to the local service and retail sectors over this nine-month period. This inbound revenue reflects sustained demand from overseas tourists visiting the country. The total sets a new high for the first nine months of the year.
stories.a: Inbound tourism consumption hit a record 7 trillion yen for the January-to-September period. Foreign visitors accelerated their outlays across retail and hospitality networks. This milestone underscores the ongoing contribution of international mobility to domestic economic activity. The aggregate marks the highest recorded spending level for these three quarters.

stories.t: Shinhan Bank Unit Tests Yen Stablecoin Pilot
stories.b: Shinhan Bank runs a part of its business in Japan called SBJ. SBJ is now testing a digital money system called a stablecoin. A stablecoin is digital money that stays tied to the value of regular money, like the yen. They are working with partner companies named JPYC and LINE NEXT for this test. The test lets users top up their digital accounts using this yen stablecoin.
stories.i: Shinhan Bank's Japan unit, SBJ, launched a proof-of-concept for yen stablecoin account top-ups. The firm partnered with JPYC and LINE NEXT to run the pilot project. This digital currency initiative explores new methods for account funding using blockchain-linked tokens pegged to the national currency. The test examines the practical application of stablecoins in retail banking.
stories.a: SBJ, the Japanese subsidiary of Shinhan Bank, initiated a proof-of-concept for yen stablecoin account top-ups in collaboration with JPYC and LINE NEXT. The pilot tests the technical infrastructure required for digital asset integration within legacy banking frameworks. This development expands experimental distributed ledger applications for local currency transactions. The trial focuses specifically on user account replenishment mechanisms.

politics.b: Japan's ruling political party is looking at new rules to stop people from trading apartments just to make a quick profit. Government ministers from different countries also met at an APEC meeting to talk about working together more closely on economic policies.
politics.i: Japan's ruling LDP is considering curbs on speculative condo trading to cool the housing market. Meanwhile, APEC finance ministers agreed to boost policy coordination during international meetings.
politics.a: The ruling LDP evaluated potential curbs on speculative condominium trading to address domestic real estate pressures. Simultaneously, APEC finance ministers committed to enhancing macroeconomic policy coordination across member jurisdictions.

stories.a: The formation of a 10 billion yuan national data group formalises state-level control over artificial intelligence inputs. stories.b: Tianjin grew its gross domestic product by 4.8% in the first three quarters. Gross domestic product measures the total value of goods and services produced. Integrated circuit output in the region surged 4.6-fold over the same period. These figures highlight regional manufacturing shifts.
stories.i: Tianjin expanded its gross domestic product by 4.8% during the first three quarters. Integrated circuit output expanded 4.6-fold across the same timeframe. Local industrial metrics demonstrate heavy concentration in semiconductor fabrication. Regional performance tracks against broader national output goals.
stories.a: Tianjin delivered a 4.8% gross domestic product expansion through the first three quarters. Integrated circuit output accelerated by 4.6 times, indicating extreme regional semiconductor clustering. This divergence between broader output and specific hardware surges skews local industrial indices.

India.label: India
India.sub: Sensex drops and Treasury bill auction yields remain zero

stories.t: Stock Indices Fall Sharply As Midcaps And Banks Slide
stories.b: The Sensex index fell by 1,400 points from its peak. Stock market values dropped by ₹8 lakh crore during the session. Banking and financial shares pulled the major benchmarks down. The India VIX measure of market volatility surged by 8%.
stories.i: The Sensex plunged 1,400 points from its intraday peak, erasing ₹8 lakh crore in market value amid broad weakness in midcap and financial equities. The India VIX jumped 8% as selling pressure intensified across multiple sectors. Banking stocks weighed heavily on the headline indices throughout the session.
stories.a: The Sensex retraced 1,400 points from its peak, accompanied by an 8% spike in the India VIX. Broad-based distribution eroded ₹8 lakh crore of market capitalization, led by severe drawdowns in midcap and banking segments. Selling pressure forced several counters, including Hero Motors and SML Mahindra, to hit their 10% lower circuits.

stories.t: Reserve Bank Of India Publishes T-Bill Results
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India offered 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day Treasury bills. Each tenor had a notified amount of ₹8,000 crore, ₹8,000 crore, and ₹7,000 crore respectively. Investors submitted competitive bids for these bills. The bank accepted nil face value for all three tenors at the auction.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India conducted Treasury bill auctions for 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day tenors with notified amounts of ₹8,000 crore, ₹8,000 crore, and ₹7,000 crore. Competitive bids arrived in volumes of 15,366.600 crore, 18,925.500 crore, and 11,352.500 crore across the maturities. The central bank ultimately accepted nil face value across all tenors.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India processed competitive bids totaling ₹15,366.600 crore for the 91-day paper, ₹18,925.500 crore for the 182-day paper, and ₹11,352.500 crore for the 364-day paper against notified amounts of ₹8,000 crore, ₹8,000 crore, and ₹7,000 crore. Despite the robust order books, the auction prints reflected zero accepted face value across all tenors with cut-off yields remaining unallocated.

stories.t: Central Bank Operates Variable Rate Repo Auction
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India held a 1-day variable rate repo auction. It notified an amount of ₹50,000 crore for banks to borrow. Banks submitted ₹93,241 crore in total bids. The central bank allotted ₹50,007 crore at a cut-off rate of 5.52%.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India executed a 1-day variable rate repo auction with a notified amount of ₹50,000 crore. Total bids received reached ₹93,241 crore. The authority allotted ₹50,007 crore at a cut-off rate and weighted average rate of 5.52%.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed liquidity demand via a 1-day variable rate repo offering targeting ₹50,000 crore. Counterparties submitted ₹93,241 crore of total bids, prompting an allotment of ₹50,007 crore. The auction cleared at a cut-off and weighted average rate of 5.52%, with a partial allotment percentage of 87.99% applied to bids at the cut-off.
